title: did2s/0.1
description: Records of Gardner's two-stage DiD as implemented by did2s for Stata (did2s.ado 0.7) and R (did2s 1.3.0), and by pyfixest's did2s (0.60.0); see spec/profiles/did2s.md. Includes did/0.1, plus: meta.estimator.method "did2s"; specification.did.treatment with comparison "untreated"; specification.options.first_stage and second_stage as written; specification.clusters (all three require a cluster variable); a default vcov of type two_stage_gmm or cluster_bootstrap that names its cluster. R and pyfixest records also meet inference/0.1 and should claim it; Stata did2s posts no residual df (normal inference), so its records claim did/0.1 and did2s/0.1 only.

first_stage.description: First-stage specification as written (fit on untreated rows only).

x-tools.did2s (Stata): first_stage() and absorb()/unit(); e(absorb) lists what was absorbed

second_stage.description: Second-stage specification as written (regression of the residualized outcome, no constant).

absorbed.description: First-stage terms absorbed as fixed effects (Stata moves plain i.x factors there).

tolerance.description: Convergence tolerance of the iterative first-stage and variance solves.

df_residual.description: Absent for Stata (normal inference). R: fixest df.residual(); pyfixest: _dfd (N - K of the second stage).

ssc.description: No tool applies a small-sample factor to the two-stage GMM matrix: record {convention, formula: "none"}. pyfixest 0.60.0 leaves the iid second stage's _ssc on the object, but it is not applied.

x-tools.did2s (R): none: crossprod(IF), passed to fixest summary(vcov =)

converged.did2s (Stata): e(converged): the first-stage and identification solves both met tolerance()
